description: A four-chambered muscular pump that moves blood through two circuits, with one-way valves between chambers.
A hollow, air-filled bone reinforced inside by thin struts, light yet stiff enough for flight.
A branching underground network that anchors a tree, absorbs water and minerals, and partners with soil fungi.
A fluid-filled sphere with a lens that focuses light onto a retina whose wiring sits in front of the light-sensing cells.
A boneless muscular limb with its own dense nerve cord and hundreds of suckers that can taste and grip.
An organ that filters blood through about a million tiny units, then reclaims most water and salts.
A silk structure of stiff radial threads and a sticky spiral, built fresh by the spider and often eaten afterward.
A colony home made of hexagonal wax cells used to store honey and pollen and to raise young.
A rock-like structure built over centuries by tiny animals living in partnership with algae inside their tissues.
Twenty-seven bones moved mostly by muscles in the forearm through long tendons, with an opposable thumb.
A deck hung from vertical cables attached to main cables draped over towers and anchored at each end.
A rigid disk or rim turning on a central axle, reducing friction when moving loads over ground.
